page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.large is an Arm-based storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by the AWS Graviton2 processor using the 64-bit Arm Neoverse-N1 core architecture running at 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores matching 2 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, accompanied by 8.0 GB of system memory, which represents a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Network baseline performance is rated at 3 Gbps, and the configuration includes no hardware GPU acceleration.

The primary differentiator of the im4gn.large configuration is its storage subsystem, bundling 937 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD capacity. Because the storage is directly attached, it eliminates standard EBS network storage latency, making it capable of handling high sequential and random I/O loads relative to its compute footprint.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest raw compute and memory throughput reflecting the dual-core profile. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU throughput reached an average score of 1519.58, while multi-core yielded 3013.28. Geekbench scores registered 945.0 for single-core and 1731.0 for multi-core. PassMark tests positioned the instance in lower percentiles for CPU (1345.31) and memory (843.03) throughput, alongside 2.35 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.25 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high local NVMe storage density per vCPU, offsetting lower overall computational execution speeds. It is well matched for mid-sized storage-bound operations including log ingestion, distributed storage nodes, caching layers, time-series data buffering, and entry-level NoSQL or relational databases requiring local NVMe endurance.
description: Amazon Web Services im4gn.large is a storage-optimized instance powered by a dual-core AWS Graviton2 Arm Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, provisioned on the AWS Nitro System. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs, 8.0 GB of system memory, and a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps, without GPU accelerators. The primary hardware asset is a bundled 937 GB local NVMe SSD, delivering high local disk density for a low-core footprint. Synthetic benchmarks reflect conservative compute throughput, yielding a Geekbench single-core score of 945.0 and multi-core score of 1731.0, paired with 2.35 million Redis SET operations per second. While multi-threaded compute and uncached memory bandwidth fall into the lower performance tiers, the instance delivers practical hardware cost efficiency for I/O-intensive workloads. It is functionally suited for intermediate database deployments, log storage systems, search indexing nodes, and distributed data pipelines needing fast direct-attached non-volatile storage.
